set.body:
When a closed path's final painted dash ends exactly on the seam, PickStroke joins
that run to the first one (PickStroke.scala, the `joined` branch, guarded by
`closed && runs.length > 1 && runs.head.head == normalized.head &&
runs.last.last == normalized.head`). The welded run turns at the start point, so a
line join is drawn there. Java2D butt-caps the two dash ends instead, and the picking
region bulges outside the painted outline by up to half the line width.

Reproduction (JVM, interaction module), no LineType.Custom required:

  pts  = Vector(P(40,50), P(58,50), P(58,60), P(40,60))   // closed, perimeter 56
  gp   = GraphicParams.unsafe(lineWidth = 4, lineCap = LineCap.Butt,
                              lineJoin = LineJoin.Round, lineType = LineType.Dashed)
  PickStroke(pts, true, gp, paintedDashes = true, miterLimit = 4)

against `new BasicStroke(4, CAP_BUTT, JOIN_ROUND, 4, Array(6f,4f), 0)
.createStrokedShape(path)` disagrees at P(39.137,48.271) and P(39.137,49.271):
picking says inside, Java2D says outside. Dashed has period 10 and 56 = 5*10 + 6, so
the last dash ends on the seam. A perimeter-60 control, where the period divides
evenly and the walk ends in an off segment, agrees everywhere.

Also reachable through the public API: Picking.fromDeviceScene with
PickPolicy(dashes = DashPicking.Painted) on a CompoundPolygon or a closed Polyline.

Found while extending StrokeOracleSuite's sweep to LineType.Custom. It predates that
work and is independent of it. The sweep's Custom pattern is deliberately chosen not
to trigger this branch, with a comment pointing here; the named rhythms still cover
the branch on the sweep paths where it agrees.

Deciding the fix needs a judgement about what is correct at a closed seam --- the
current behaviour carries a deliberate-looking comment, and the neighbouring
PickingSuite case "a single dash covering a closed path keeps endpoint caps at its
coincident seam" cites Java2D and Chromium 141 --- so it should be settled against
both renderers rather than against Java2D alone.
set.title: PickStroke's closed-seam dash join disagrees with the Java2D outline
